article.content: Spurs off bottom after first win against Coventry Lampard unhappy Marmoush goal stood Roberto De Zerbi said that Tottenham are playing with more togetherness after holding a clear-the-air meeting before their recent game with Manchester United. Spurs went on to draw 1-1 with 10 men against United and are out of the bottom three after beating Coventry 3-1 at home on Monday night. De Zerbi felt the performance against Coventry could have been better but was happy with his side’s attitude as they claimed their first Premier League win of the season. Continue reading...
article.aiArticle:
Tottenham Hotspur have climbed off the bottom of the Premier League standings following a much-needed victory over Coventry, a turnaround that manager Roberto De Zerbi attributes to a candid squad meeting and a team bonding excursion. 

According to Sport | The Guardian, the clear-the-air talks took place ahead of the club's fixture against Manchester United. De Zerbi indicated that these frank discussions, paired with a subsequent team trip, fostered a renewed sense of unity within the squad, helping players connect on a deeper level and transforming the atmosphere in the dressing room into something resembling a close-knit family.

## Rising Out of the Relegation Zone

The recent results mark a significant shift for a side that had previously struggled to find its footing. Earlier in the season, evaluations highlighted that [Spurs 'lack confidence' but we are a good team - De Zerbi](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/spurs-lack-confidence-but-we-are-a-good-team-de-zerbi), underscoring the psychological hurdles the manager needed to clear. The victory over Coventry provided tangible proof of progress, particularly as key performers stepped up on the pitch, evidenced by how [Maddison shines on return - Tottenham v Coventry ratings](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/maddison-shines-on-return-tottenham-v-coventry-ratings) during the hard-fought encounter. 

Not everyone was entirely satisfied with the weekend's proceedings, however. Following the match, opposing manager Frank Lampard voiced clear frustration over a controversial decision to let an Omar Marmoush goal stand, a call that heavily influenced the contest's final outcome according to the report.

## Context and Stakes

> **Context:** Premier League management is a high-stakes environment where slow starts routinely cost managers their jobs and plunge clubs into financial jeopardy. For Tottenham, moving away from the relegation danger zone alleviates mounting pressure on the coaching staff and restores calm among supporters who demand European-caliber performances. When squads fracture during difficult runs, internal communication exercises like clear-the-air meetings represent a standard last line of defense before the January transfer window opens.

## What to Watch

> **Context:** Observers will be monitoring whether this newfound cohesion translates into sustained consistency over the busy autumn fixture schedule. Analysts note that upcoming matches against top-tier opponents will truly test if the psychological boost from the bonding trip can sustain a lasting climb up the table.

Sources: [Sport | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/19/players-meeting-and-bonding-trip-have-boosted-tottenham-says-de-zerbi)
